focus_area: Bulk pipeline deep coverage: SPEC 6.2.3 (QueueBulkAiSummaryJobs optional job input + fail-fast ordering), SPEC 6.3 (BulkGenerateAiSummariesJob#each_iteration claim-row fix), bulk controller job: threading, and SPEC 12 bulk-related test expectations (second-opinion redundant coverage)

findings.title: Untraceable test-only edits in bulk controller spec: rescore_requested merge-reconciliation changes beyond SPEC 12's stated scope
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC 12 / 13 authorize, for spec/controllers/api/v1/bulk_ai_job_application_summaries_controller_spec.rb, only: (a) updating the hash_including expectation at lines 72-77 for the new job: input, and (b) zero-criteria 422 coverage. Layer 1 rule: every change in the diff must trace to SPEC / DECISIONS / Reviewed Plan / an adjudicated ruling; the dispatch note states anything visible in git diff develop...HEAD is branch work.
findings.evidence: Full scope, all in spec/controllers/api/v1/bulk_ai_job_application_summaries_controller_spec.rb: lines 57, 96, 107, 123 add rescore_requested: false to four PRE-EXISTING examples' post params (all_stages happy path, cross-org RecordNotFound, interactor-failure 422, forbidden 403); line 76 reshapes the pre-existing expectation from top-level rescore_requested: 'true' to params: hash_including('rescore_requested' => 'true') - a restructure beyond the authorized job: kind_of(Job) addition on line 74. Introduced in merge commit 68e5e6a4e ('Merge develop into job-criteria-settings'), not in feature commit ee6b07c75 or conventions commit 9ed954142. Root cause verified: develop commit d9f08ec5d (PR #3054) made rescore_requested a required param (bulk_params.require(:rescore_requested), develop controller) and moved it into the params: context input, but left develop's own spec examples stale - at the merge-base (639458b9d, develop tip), four examples post without the required param (would raise ActionController::ParameterMissing) and the line-75 expectation asserts a top-level rescore_requested: input the develop controller no longer passes, so develop's spec file is red on develop itself. The branch repaired develop's breakage as part of merge reconciliation. Test-only; no production code rides along; the merge commit message documents the reconciliation. But no SPEC/DECISIONS/plan text or adjudicated ruling covers these edits, so under Layer 1 rules they are untraceable branch work.
findings.recommendation: Adjudicate and ratify the merge-reconciliation spec edits explicitly (record in ORCHESTRATION-LOG so later rounds do not re-flag). Do NOT revert them: they are mechanically required for the pre-existing examples to pass against develop's required-param contract - reverting leaves the suite red with ParameterMissing and a never-matching receive(:call).with expectation. If the adjudicator declines to ratify, the alternative is pushing the fix upstream to develop, not removing it from this branch.

spec_coverage.notes: All assigned requirements are implemented and behaviorally correct. (1) Claim-row fix at app/jobs/bulk_generate_ai_summaries_job.rb:62-66 matches the SPEC 6.3 block plus the adjudicated Rails.logger.error line (conventions-pass item 2); NO transaction block exists anywhere in the job file, so update_columns(status: :failed) at line 64 is outside any transaction, consistent with the sibling writes at lines 56, 72, 92. (2) Guard at app/interactors/queue_bulk_ai_summary_jobs.rb:19 uses the exact SPEC message, sits directly after the credits fail! per SPEC 6.2.3, and fires before the scope query (line 21), SubmitResumeToTextractJob kickoffs (lines 29-31), claim-row creation (lines 67-78), and the BulkGenerateAiSummariesJob enqueue (line 85) - Interactor fail! raises, so zero claim rows can be written when it fires; verified by the queue spec asserting BulkAiSummaryJobApplication.where(...).to be_empty. (3) Grep confirms QueueBulkAiSummaryJobs has no callers beyond the two controller actions (both now pass job: @job); the optional/safe-nav input is directly exercised by the job-less-call test at spec/interactors/queue_bulk_ai_summary_jobs_spec.rb:222-235. (4) Falsifiability verified for every new/modified test: reverting the each_iteration fix leaves the claim row 'processing' and fails the :failed assertions at spec/jobs/bulk_generate_ai_summaries_job_spec.rb:81 and :126; removing the ValidateAiSummaryGeneration zero-criteria guard makes the zero-criteria batch run the real pipeline to the funnel guard, marking the row :done and broadcasting AI_SUMMARY_BULK_COMPLETE instead of FAILED (test fails) - and create_credit_test_job supplies a description (spec/support/ai_credits_test_helpers.rb:96), so validation genuinely reaches the zero-criteria check rather than failing earlier; removing the interactor guard makes the queue-spec zero-criteria test fail (proceeds and either enqueues or NoMethodErrors on the absent params input); dropping job: from the controller makes the kind_of(Job) message expectations fail. No ghost tests: all assertions are behavioral (DB status, HTTP status, exact error body, have_been_enqueued, broadcast args, mailer delivery). Two observations, not findings: the zero-criteria batch test's payload contains a single claim row, so SPEC 12's 'all rows :failed' is exercised with n=1 (the per-row each_iteration path is what is under test; a multi-row batch would add little since rows are processed independently and validation failure does not raise); the new describe '#create' block in the controller spec traces to SPEC 12's 'both actions' requirement (develop's file covered only #all_stages, so #create coverage had to be added to assert job: threading and the 422 on both actions).
